title: Oily skin, sunscreen and serum on a student budget

parts: Hi, I'm Om Dwivedi, 22, final-year student living in Andheri, Mumbai. My face gets super oily by afternoon and I keep getting pimples on my chin and forehead. Monsoon humidity makes it worse. Where do I even start?
Hi Om. For oily, acne-prone skin a simple routine works best: gentle gel cleanser, light moisturiser, and sunscreen every morning. Add one active at a time so you can tell what helps.
Right now I just wash with whatever face wash my brother left, then nothing. No moisturiser because I feel it will make me oilier.
Skipping moisturiser can actually make skin produce more oil. A gel or water-based one is fine for oily skin. Start with a mild cleanser and a lightweight gel moisturiser.
My budget is tight yaar, I can spend maybe ₹500 per month on skincare in total. Pocket money plus a little from tuitions.
That's workable. Prioritise cleanser, sunscreen and one active. Many Indian D2C brands have good options under ₹400 each, so you can rotate rather than buy everything at once.
My friend Priya swears by niacinamide for oil control. She uses the Minimalist 10% one. Is that okay for someone my age?
Niacinamide at 5 to 10% is commonly used for oil control and marks. Start with 5% if your skin is sensitive, use it once a day, and patch test first.
Priya paid ₹599 for the 30ml bottle on Nykaa. That's more than my entire monthly budget lol. Is there any cheaper way to try it?
Yes: look for 5% versions or smaller 10ml sizes, which are often around ₹250 to ₹350. Also compare prices on Amazon and the brand sites, since discounts vary.
Okay. Also my other friend Rahul says I should just use Multani mitti and lemon. Is that a good idea?
I'd avoid lemon on the face, it can irritate and cause dark patches in the sun. Multani mitti occasionally is okay, but it can dry skin out. A proper cleanser and sunscreen are safer.
Fine, no lemon. Can I also ask, how long before I see results with a serum? I get impatient.
Usually 4 to 8 weeks for oil and texture, longer for marks. Take a photo in the same light today so you can compare honestly later.
My number is +91 98200 12345 if you can send me a routine PDF, otherwise just type it here.

I can't send files or messages to phone numbers, but here is a simple routine in text. Morning: cleanser, light moisturiser, sunscreen SPF 50. Night: cleanser, moisturiser, and the serum on alternate days to begin with.

Back again. I started the cleanser, now need a sunscreen. It has to be non-greasy because of Mumbai heat. I looked at Minimalist SPF 50, Dot & Key watermelon SPF 50 and Deconstruct SPF 50. Which one for oily skin?

All three are lightweight gels or fluids. Minimalist and Deconstruct tend to feel matte and are fragrance free, Dot & Key is fruitier in scent. For acne-prone skin, fragrance-free and non-comedogenic is the safer pick.
Prices on Nykaa: Minimalist ₹399, Deconstruct ₹449, Dot & Key ₹495. All slightly above what I wanted to spend. The Derma Co has one at ₹349 too.
The Derma Co's gel sunscreen is cheaper and well reviewed for oily skin. Check the amount in grams, since a cheaper tube may hold less product, and compare the price per 50 g.
Hmm, good point, Minimalist is 50g for ₹399 and the Derma Co one is 50g for ₹349. So Derma Co is cheaper but more people complain of a white cast, right?
Some reviewers do mention a slight cast on deeper skin tones. If you are wheatish you may notice it less with a gel-cream formula. A sample or small size would settle it.
I added the Minimalist SPF and the 10% niacinamide serum to my Nykaa cart. Total came to ₹998 and then ₹60 shipping fee because I'm below the free shipping limit. That is too much, I'm leaving it.
That's a sensible call if it breaks your monthly limit. Options: buy one product now, pick a store with free shipping, or wait for a sale. Which one matters most to you this month?
Sunscreen matters more I think. But even ₹399 plus ₹60 shipping feels bad. Let me check Amazon.
Amazon often has lower prices with free delivery on larger orders, but check the seller is the official brand store to avoid fakes.
On Amazon the Minimalist sunscreen is ₹379 with free delivery for Prime only. I don't have Prime. Without it delivery is ₹40. So basically same thing. Ugh.
Then the saving is small. If the brand website runs a free shipping threshold, a combined order with a friend could split the fee.
Maybe I'll ask Priya to order with me. She also wants the sunscreen. But then I wait for her paycheque, can't do right now. I closed the tab and abandoned the cart for now.
That's fine, nothing is lost. Cart prices can change though, so note the product names rather than relying on the saved cart.
Also I looked at the Dot & Key serum, 10ml for ₹445 but it's a vitamin C one. Too expensive for a small bottle honestly. I don't think it's worth it for me.
Per ml that is costly. Since your goal is oil control and marks, niacinamide gives better value for your budget than vitamin C right now.
I tried a friend's Derma Co sunscreen for two days at college near Bandra and it felt okay, not sticky. Slight white cast but fine in the shade.
Good to know. Two days is a short trial, so watch for new bumps over a week. If it suits you, the Derma Co one fits your budget best.
Honestly the thing I want is a small trial pack. I don't want to commit ₹400 on something that might break me out.
Trial or travel sizes exist for several brands, usually 15 to 30 ml, and that is a very reasonable way to test oily-skin products before buying a full tube.
Yeah, a ₹199 mini would be perfect. Why don't brands make that more often? Even for travel I'd buy it.
Smaller packs cost brands more per ml, so they often skip them. But demand from students on tight budgets is real, and some brands do launch minis when asked.

Update: I finally ordered. Found a Minimalist 5% niacinamide mini 10ml on Amazon for ₹249 with free delivery on a ₹499 order, so I added a 30ml gel cleanser to cross the limit. Total ₹499. Is that smart?
That works well: the mini lets you test without a big spend, and the cleanser is something you need anyway. Just make sure the sellers are the official brand stores.
I paid with UPI, my email for the order is om.dwivedi.demo@example.com. The order arrives Thursday in Andheri.
Great, keep your order confirmation. When it arrives, patch test the serum on your jaw for a couple of nights before using it on your whole face.
The mini arrived. Patch test done, no redness. Using it at night on alternate days like you said, plus the cleanser. Sunscreen I still use Priya's Derma Co until I buy my own.
Sounds like a careful approach. Sunscreen is the single most important step, so prioritise buying your own SPF soon, in small amounts if possible.
After 10 days my oiliness is a bit lower and fewer new pimples. Not a miracle but honestly noticeable. Rahul asked what I changed.
That timeline matches expectations. Keep photos monthly and stay consistent. Avoid adding another active just yet.
Now the 10ml is nearly done. A full 30ml is ₹599 which is too expensive for me, I would only buy the mini again. Any alternative at a lower price?
Compare per ml: other brands at 10% niacinamide in 20ml packs sit near ₹350 to ₹450. The Derma Co and Deconstruct both have options. Check ingredient percentages, not just the brand name.
I'll probably repurchase the ₹249 mini and a ₹349 Derma Co sunscreen next month. That fits ₹500 if I skip one thing. Is the order okay?
Yes, sunscreen first, then a serum refill. If a sale drops the price, buy then. You're building a good routine at a sensible cost.
One last thing, would I recommend all this to my cousin? Yes, mostly the sunscreen and the mini serum, but I'd tell her to avoid paying shipping and to start small.
That is solid advice: start small, patch test, and track results over several weeks.
